It is believed that approximately 40% of the total GDP output of Jamaica today is within the [[Informal economy|informal markets]].<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://publications.iadb.org/en/publication/11174/informal-sector-jamaica|title=The Informal Sector in Jamaica|journal=Idb Publications|date=December 2006 |access-date=2019-12-01 |last1=Torero |first1=Máximo |last2=Robles |first2=Miguel |last3=Hernández |first3=Manuel |last4=Roca |first4=Jorge De la |last5=Webber |first5=Maureen |last6=Thomas |first6=Desmond |doi=10.18235/0008747 }}</ref> Several economist have voiced concern over this, arguing that an increase in the size of the informal economy can lead to a decline in economic growth.<ref>{{Cite journal |first1=Chantal |last1=Wedderburn |first2=Eric P. |last2=Chiang |first3=Rupert |last3=Rhodd |date=January 2012|title=The informal economy in Jamaica: Is it feasible to tax this sector?|url=https://monroecollege.edu/uploadedFiles/_Site_Assets/PDF/The_informal_economy_in_Jamaica.pdf|journal=Journal of International Business and Cultural Studies|volume=6}}</ref>{{pred |date=July 2024}} Today Jamaica has a [[List of countries and dependencies by population|population]] of 2.8 million individuals (2018),<ref name=":1" /> a [[GNI per capita]] of $4,990 (2018), and a lower inequality rate than most nations in [[Latin America]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/NY.GNP.PCAP.CD?locations=JM&most_recent_value_desc=false&year_high_desc=true|title=GNI per capita, Atlas method (current US$) – Jamaica {{!}} Data|website=data.worldbank.org|access-date=2019-12-01}}</ref><ref name=":2" />  The current GDP is 15.71 billion US Dollars,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.CD?locations=JM |title=GDP (current US$) – Jamaica |website=The World Bank |access-date=2019-12-01}}</ref> making Jamaica one of the largest [[Economy of the Caribbean|economies in the Caribbean]].  The economy of Jamaica consists mostly of a service sector, contributing over 70% of the GDP.<ref name=":1" /> Tourism accounts for 20% of GDP, and [[remittance]]s accounts for 14%.<ref name=":1" /> The Jamaican economy has suffered from poor overall growth in the past several decades, averaging less than 1% growth annually over the past 30 years.<ref name=":1" />  Some of the causes of slow growth in Jamaica are a disproportionately large public sector, high crime levels, endemic corruption, strict regulation, poor judicial effectiveness, a high [[debt-to-GDP ratio]], and high levels of unemployment.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heritage.org/index/country/jamaica|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090115142726/http://www.heritage.org/index/country/Jamaica|url-status=unfit|archive-date=January 15, 2009|title=Jamaica Economy: Population, GDP, Inflation, Business, Trade, FDI, Corruption|website=www.heritage.org|language=en|access-date=2019-12-01}}</ref>  The economy of Jamaica is highly susceptible to fluctuations in weather condition, especially hurricanes (See list of [[:Category:Hurricanes in Jamaica|Hurricanes in Jamaica]]).  However, after implementing economic reforms as part of program supported by the [[International Monetary Fund]] (IMF), [[World Bank Group|The World Bank Group]] and the [[Inter-American Development Bank|Inter-American Development bank]] (IADB), economic stability was established, and Jamaica has achieved 16 consecutive quarters of growth.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/opinion/2019/05/16/jamaica-has-made-an-extraordinary-economic-turnaround|title=Jamaica has made an|website=World Bank|language=en|access-date=2019-12-01}}</ref>
